quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: You can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position keeps you safe. It should help you see and be seen, avoid hazards, and escape danger. Your position should discourage other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean with the operator as they lean.
Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the operator as they lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean the same way. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: As a beginning rider following another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Keep at least a four-second distance between you and the other vehicle.
Get as close to the other vehicle as possible.
Always ride in the left part of your lane so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep at least a four-second distance between you and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should maintain at least a four-second following distance. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before entering a turn. If you must change gears during a turn, do it smoothly.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, they should:

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders passing at the same time.

questions.explanation: When a group of riders passes on a two-lane road, each rider should pass one at a time. One rider must finish passing before the next rider starts.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Protects your entire face, not just your eyes.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your entire face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your whole face and eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection by itself.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down to approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: Downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then accelerate and ride away from it. If a larger animal chases you, brake and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You can complete the pass in a no passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You may exceed the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be completed within the posted speed limit and only in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you balance. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handlebars.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Encourage other friends to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
Slow down their pace of drinking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: To prevent someone from driving while drunk, arrange other transportation, involve them in other activities to slow their drinking, and get other friends to help. Never tell them it is okay to drive on less-crowded roads.

questions.question: Which provides the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: When packing a load on a motorcycle, where should heavier items go?

options.text: Lighter items should be stored in front of you.

questions.explanation: Pack heavier items toward the front. Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. How can you reduce your crash risk?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.

questions.explanation: Make yourself as visible as possible by wearing bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: When transporting a passenger, what should they do?

options.text: Sit as far back on the seat as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should lean the same way you lean. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When being passed, which is NOT a potential hazard?

options.text: Objects being thrown from other vehicles.

questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the vehicle's mirrors. Be aware of wind gusts and objects that may be thrown. Headlights are not a hazard when being passed.

questions.question: When should a passenger mount the motorcycle?

options.text: Sit as close to the rear as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should get on only after the engine has started and the transmission is in neutral. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control and should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the rear brake on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter the road conditions.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to driving a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
A motorcycle is easier to see than a car.
You should pass on the shoulder, not the main road.
You must make eye contact with other drivers when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller than cars. Other drivers may not see you or you may disappear into their blind spot. Being seen is more important on a motorcycle than in a car.

questions.question: To be more visible at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride very close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: The best way to help others see you at an intersection is to keep your headlight on. Your headlight should always be on when your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: Your lane position should help you:

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
Prevent other drivers from passing you.
Stay in other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: A good lane position protects your lane and tells other drivers what you plan to do next.

questions.question: A major effect of drinking alcohol is:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down your body and brain. It makes you think and move more slowly.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's space cushion:

options.text: Should change based on road and traffic conditions.
Is not needed in most situations.
Should be avoided to keep traffic moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should change based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Give yourself more space when it is wet or slippery, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy. These conditions increase your stopping distance.
